chapter: Donaldsonville, family and Richard M. Jones
title: Drummer Bolegs (Andrew Barnett) and Joe Walker
summary: Bolegs' skill at catching film effects on drums versus rudimental drummer Joe Walker.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, no, I was thinking about back up there in Donaldsonville. Donaldsonville, I... Because there's some people I never didn't know about. I heard about Bolegs.
Bolegs. Bolegs from St. James, Louisiana. Mm-hmm. Who was he? His name, right name is Andrew Barnett. Oh, yeah?
Ha, ha, ha, ha. I just didn't know anything about him. What did he play? Drum. Was he any good?
Woo! He was the greatest drummer... One of the greatest drummers in the South. They had two up there. They had him and they had Joe Walker. You ever heard of Joe Walker?
I've heard the name, but I can't place him. I'm thinking about a saxophone. And he was a good drummer, Joe Walker, huh?

Joe Walker was a rudiment drummer. Clyde know what I'm talking about. He mostly played, he played everything by music, rudiments. Everything was rudiments. But Boleg was a man that, he used to go in the picture show and those days they didn't have no sound pictures and he'd catch everything that'd go on. He had everything on the drums, all kinds of things. See, like a man be, you know, somebody be whistling on the television, he'd whistle. In the movie? Yeah, crickets. Yeah. Yeah, he'd catch that. He used to have pit bands. Yeah, I know. We were back when I was going to the show. A lot of traps. Yeah, yeah, everything around.
